description: Published Ca II H&K transient (exocomet) absorption events, compiled 2026-11-21 for the pre-registered scorecard. All numbers read from the primary papers (text, tables, figures). Values marked ‘read from figure’ are approximate (+/- one histogram bin / a few per cent).

sources.citation: Kiefer F., Lecavelier des Etangs A., Boissier J., Vidal-Madjar A., Beust H., Lagrange A.-M., Hebrard G., Ferlet R., 2014, Nature, 514, 462-464, ‘Two families of exocomets in the beta Pictoris system’
sources.ads_or_doi: doi:10.1038/nature13849 (2014Natur.514..462K); read from the accepted manuscript hosted by ESO (eso1432a.pdf), no arXiv version

sources.citation: Kiefer F., Lecavelier des Etangs A., Augereau J.-C., Vidal-Madjar A., Lagrange A.-M., Beust H., 2014, A&A, 561, L10, ‘Exocomets in the circumstellar gas disk of HD 172555’
Bendahan-West R., Kennedy G. M., Brown D. J. A., Strom P. A., 2025, MNRAS, 537, 229-251, ‘Quantifying spectroscopic Ca II exocomet transit occurrence in two decades of HARPS data’
sources.ads_or_doi: doi:10.1093/mnras/stae2804; arXiv:2412.13253 (v1 text used; check the published version for any changed numbers)

ranges._scope: Envelope over the entries in per_star only (confirmed / Tier 1 events: beta Pic from kiefer2014nature, HD 172555 from kiefer2014hd172555 and bendahanwest2025). Tier 2 candidates are kept separately in per_star_unconfirmed and are NOT in this envelope. All envelopes are HARPS-only (R ~ 115,000).

velocity_kms.source: kiefer2014nature (envelope set by beta Pic; HD 172555 lies inside)
velocity_kms.note: Relative to the star (stellar rest frame), positive = redshift (gas moving towards the star along the line of sight, i.e. away from the observer). Kiefer 2014 Nature text: ‘radial velocities ranging from -150 to +200 km/s with respect to the beta Pictoris heliocentric radial velocity (20 km/s)’. The fitted statistical sample (Fig. 3b) spans only about -110 to +180 km/s (read from figure). Population S: v_r = 36 +/- 55; population D: 15 +/- 6 km/s (mean +/- s.d.).

depth_K.source: kiefer2014nature (both ends set by beta Pic; HD 172555 0.029-0.072 lies inside)
depth_K.note: Fractional depth p_K of a Gaussian fitted to F_obs/F_ref (F_ref = the star’s own reference spectrum), i.e. relative to the local stellar+CS flux at that velocity, 0-1. The minimum 0.01 is the selection cut, not a measured property: features with p below 0.01 and dv below 3 km/s were discarded. Max ~0.97 is read from Extended Data Fig. 4 (approximate). Split: population S p_K below 0.4, population D p_K above 0.4.

fwhm_kms.note: Gaussian FWHM in velocity units. The min 3 km/s is the selection cut and the HARPS resolution limit, not a measured property. Max ~100 km/s is read from Fig. 3a (the histogram runs to the axis edge at 100; values beyond 100 not shown). Population S: 55 +/- 55; population D: 7 +/- 3 km/s (mean +/- s.d.).

ratio_K_over_H.source: kiefer2014nature (Methods Eqs. 6-8; ED Fig. 4) and kiefer2014hd172555
ratio_K_over_H.note: Depth ratio p_K/p_H. These are the physical limits: 1 = saturated/optically thick, 2 = optically thin, for the f_K = 2 f_H Ca II doublet. Kiefer 2014 Nature fit both lines at once with p_K = alpha(1-exp(-A)), p_H = alpha(1-exp(-A/2)). The beta Pic points in ED Fig. 4 fill this band, between the p_K = p_H line and the alpha = 1 curve. No per-event ratio list is published.

duration_hours.note: NOT measured per-event transit durations. Kiefer 2014 Nature: the features vary ‘on timescales of one to six hours’; ‘variations were typically not seen on timescales less than 30 minutes (corresponding to the minimum duration of a transit)’. HD 172555 has only lower limits (minimum durations of 3 min to 3.5 h, Kiefer 2014 A&A Table 2) and a 3.5 h to 450 d bracket (Bendahan-West 2025). These are consistent with the range but do not set it.

per_star.where: Velocity: main text p.1-2 and Methods ‘Fitting method’. Depth: Methods Eqs. 5-8, selection cut p.2, max read from Extended Data Fig. 4. FWHM: cut p.2, max read from Fig. 3a. Ratio: Methods Eqs. 6-8 and ED Fig. 4. Timescales: p.1 and Methods.
per_star.n_events: 1106 spectra (2003-2011), averaged into 357 spectra (10-min bins, S/N above 80) with ~6 features per spectrum (~6000 signatures). One spectrum per night gives 570 independent clouds, 493 after the depth/width cut. Clouds with alpha = 1 were also excluded from the statistics.
per_star.caveats: Excluded the CS-line core (+/-3 km/s around 21 km/s systemic) from the analysis. Depths are relative to an empirical reference spectrum built from the upper flux envelope of all 1106 spectra.

per_star.where: Table 3 (7 fitted spectra from 4 epochs: 22/09/04 x2, 21/08/05, 08/07/10, 11/06/11 x3). Table 2 minimum durations. Sect. 3.2.
per_star.n_events: 4 epochs with FEB detections in 129 HARPS spectra (2004-2011), 22 nights.
per_star.notes: Velocity: Table 3 values cluster at ~0, and the text calls the 21/08/05 event ‘redshifted ... 13 km/s’ with ‘FEBs mostly seen at the star radial velocity’ (star at +2 km/s heliocentric). So they are read as relative to the star, although Table 3 does not state its frame explicitly. Depth: ‘K line Depth’ from fits to F_obs/F_ref (local fractional). FWHM: 08/07/10 is 18.4 (+7.9/-10.1). 21/08/05 (38.4) may be two blended components (text). Ratio: no K/H column is given. The values were DERIVED here from Table 3 optical depth A using p_K/p_H = (1-exp(-A))/(1-exp(-A/2)): A = 0.061 gives 1.97, A = 1.90 gives 1.39, and the 08/07/10 upper limit A of about 10.3 allows down to ~1.0. The text agrees qualitatively: 2004 K ~2x deeper than H, while in 2011 ‘H almost as deep as K’. Duration: only lower limits (‘Minimum duration’ = time between first and last detection), 3.5 h (22/09/04), 1.9 h (11/06/11), 3 min (21/08/05 and 08/07/10). The 11/06/11 event was not seen the next day, so its timescale is under 1 day (text).

raw_values.same_night_average: -3.5 sigma, 4 km/s, W 2 km/s, depth 10%, 333 d (Table 4 footnote a)

per_star.notes: Velocity: BW25 RVs are BERV-corrected and have NO systemic correction. The star-relative value is 4 - 2 = +2 km/s, using the star RV of 2 km/s quoted in the paper. Depth: BW25 ‘Depth (%)’ is relative to spectra normalised by the mean flux at +/-(200-700) km/s, i.e. a pseudo-continuum, NOT the local stellar flux. The paper calls these depths ‘only approximate’, so set to null here (raw 10%). W: the number of consecutive ~1 km/s pixels with SNR below -3 sigma, not a FWHM, so null here. Duration: text gives 3h30 to 450 days (450 d = 10800 h; a bracket, not a measurement). Table 4 gives dt_max = 0.008 d and footnote a gives 333 d, which are internally inconsistent with the text. Recovers one of the Kiefer 2014 A&A 22/09/04 (21-09-2004 UT) detections.

per_star_unconfirmed.where: Table 4; Sect. 4.3 (star RV ‘approx 25 km/s’ quoted in text)
per_star_unconfirmed.notes: M2V; single spectrum; no H counterpart
G3/5V; single spectrum; no H counterpart; systemic RV not given in paper
K5V; single spectrum; depth above 100% (negative flux, noise plus signal, per text); text typo ‘HIP 5159’
O9.5V; H counterparts present; near-constant RV over years, so possibly not exocometary (O-star variability)
